topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture's learning objectives, the historical context of cancer hallmarks, and the progression model of tumorigenesis.

topics.label: Sustained proliferative signaling and insensitivity to growth inhibitors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in key signaling cascades, such as Wnt/beta-catenin, receptor tyrosine kinases, and TGF-beta, promote cell cycle entry and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation block in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics illustrate how cancers in hematopoietic lineages and solid epithelial tissues prevent progenitor cells from achieving terminal differentiation.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: It examines how alterations in p53 and the balance between pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins allow cancer cells to evade programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, telomeres, and senescence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how telomere erosion triggers protective senescence responses and how cancer cells bypass these barriers by upregulating telomerase.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the metabolic rewiring of cancer cells, including the Warburg effect and the epigenetic consequences of Krebs cycle enzyme mutations.

topics.label: Inducing tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the requirement for new blood vessel growth to sustain tumor survival and how the angiogenic balance shifts during tumor development.

topics.label: Invasion, circulation, and metastatic colonization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biological steps, anatomical routes, clinical monitoring, and clonal genetics involved in cancer metastasis.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and summary
topics.groupedBecause: It provides closing framing on the integration of cancer hallmarks, references further reading, and concludes the session.
